paragraphs.source_en: directions on the p-branes come together at some point, they can create a peak so great that a bit of the p-brane breaks away and goes off as a particle. Thus the p-branes can absorb and emit particles like black holes (Fig. 4. 2 3 ). One can regard the p-branes as an effective theory; that is, while we don't need to believe that there actually are little sheets moving through a flat spacetime, black holes can behave as if they were made up of such sheets. It is like water, which is made up of billions and billions of H 0 molecules with complicated interactions.
